confirmedRules.name: Small corner radii are derived from a single radius token

confirmedRules.when: a rounded-md or rounded-sm element is rendered
confirmedRules.then: rounded-md = calc(8px - 2px) = 6px and rounded-sm = calc(8px - 4px) = 4px; rounded-lg = var(--radius) = 8px

confirmedRules.name: Live OS theme changes are honoured only without an explicit user preference

confirmedRules.when: The OS color-scheme media query fires its 'change' event
confirmedRules.then: nothing happens — the saved preference keeps the theme fixed

confirmedRules.name: One theme wipe transition at a time; clicks during a transition are dropped
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Rapid repeated clicks on the theme toggle do not stack overlapping wipe animations — only the first click is acted on until the current transition finishes.
confirmedRules.given: A wipe transition is in progress (running === true)
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks the theme toggle again before the transition completes
confirmedRules.then: the click is silently discarded — wipeTheme returns immediately and the theme does not change

The lock is a module-level variable, so it is per-page not per-button

confirmedRules.name: Transition lock is always released, with a hard timeout backstop
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The theme toggle can never get permanently stuck: the lock is released when the animation reports it finished, and unconditionally after 1.5 seconds no matter what.
confirmedRules.given: A wipe transition was started and the lock flag has been set
confirmedRules.when: Either transition.finished settles, or 1500 ms elapse without it
confirmedRules.then: running is reset to false, any pending timer is cleared, and the data-theme-transition attribute is removed from the root element
confirmedRules.parameters: Timeout = 1500 ms (line 65); cleanup clears releaseTimer and deletes root.dataset.themeTransition (lines 46-53); release is also called on a startViewTransition throw (line 71)
edgeCases: release() is idempotent — it may run twice (timer then finished) and clearing an undefined timer is guarded by the `!== undefined` check
If startViewTransition is absent the lock is never taken, so the timeout path is not used either

confirmedRules.name: Animation is skipped when unsupported or when reduced motion is requested
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The wipe animation only runs where the browser supports view transitions and the user has not asked for reduced motion; otherwise the theme still switches, just instantly.
confirmedRules.given: document.startViewTransition is not a function, OR the media query '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' matches
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks the theme toggle
confirmedRules.then: setTheme(next) is called directly with no lock, no data-theme-transition attribute, and no animation
confirmedRules.parameters: Capability check captured once at load: canWipe = typeof document.startViewTransition === 'function' (line 42); reduced-motion query = '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' (line 6)
edgeCases: canWipe is evaluated once at script load, so a browser that gains the API later is never upgraded in this page session
reducedMotion.matches is read at click time, so toggling the OS setting takes effect without reload

confirmedRules.name: Toggle flips to the opposite of the currently applied theme
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A click on the theme toggle sets the theme to the opposite of whatever is currently on screen, and the toggle button only becomes clickable after the page is parsed.
confirmedRules.given: The root element currently carries the class 'light'
confirmedRules.then: wipeTheme('dark') is requested, i.e. the next theme is derived from the committed DOM class rather than from the stored preference
confirmedRules.parameters: Next value derived from root.classList.contains('light') (line 80); handler is attached inside a DOMContentLoaded listener registered with { once: true } (lines 77-82)
edgeCases: Deriving from the DOM class means that if the DOM class and the stored preference ever diverge (the storage-event handler updates preference then reapplies), the click still targets the visible opposite
The click listener is bound once and never rebound, so the button element must exist at DOMContentLoaded

A control that the regulated action can bypass is not a billing-consent obligation in code; it is UI friction.
- No derived or computed value. Nothing is calculated, no rate or rounding, no eligibility record. It is a two-step acknowledgment, i.e. "merely one of many validations," which the P0 bar explicitly excludes.
- The threshold is arbitrary and cosmetic. 4000 ms is a UX dwell window, not a policy constant; no dollar amount, tax, retention period, or reporting figure derives from it. Changing it to 2000 ms or removing it entirely alters no transaction, ledger entry, or regulatory artifact.
- Bypassable by design and by accident. A reload, a second tab, or the 4 s timeout all produce the same billed outcome the confirmation was meant to gate; the persistence layer records only status/progress reset (app.py:358).

The genuinely money-relevant rule sits upstream at app.py:351-367 — resume re-runs the online engine (`online_engine=engine_kind_from_name(t.engine)`, 365), re-uploads audio, and re-bills — plus the resumable predicate `(not running) and t.status in {"pending","running","failed"}` (app.py:171). Rating it P0 would make every modernization phase prove equivalence of a label swap and a timer, while the actual cost-incurring endpoint goes unpinned.

The onClick `costs && !confirming ? setConfirming(true) : onResume()` (926) gives exactly "online: first click arms, second click within window resumes; offline: first click resumes immediately". The destructive variant (925), label swap 确认续跑 (928), and warning text 在线续跑会重新上传音频并按量计费 (930) all check out. The gate `t.resumable && ...` is one line off — the card says task.tsx:1160 and the render guard is indeed at 1160 (the section itself starts 1153); minor, but the GWT "only rendered when resumable" is faithful. Backend corroborates the cost premise: resume_task (src/transcript/web/app.py:351-366) re-submits the whole source with the same task_id, and test_pipeline.py:299 confirms only undone chunks are skipped — so re-upload/re-bill for unfinished segments is real. No injection-shaped content in the cited lines. P0 justification fails: the rule is a client-side UX friction guard (a second click + two strings). The money-moving behavior is the backend skip-done-chunks invariant, and while the confirmation reduces accidental re-spend, it enforces nothing — it does not move money itself, guard a regulatory requirement, or protect data integrity; it is one UI safeguard among many. Per the P0 bar ("merely one of many validations is not P0"), this belongs at P1. Hovering behind it, the actual P0 here is "resume skips done chunks and does not repay", which is not the cited rule.) — confirm criticality.
